forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: today is the flattest day of the fortnight and tomorrow is the best — brutal timing. Right now the ocean has almost nothing in it: 2.0ft @ 3s of WNW wind chop (297°) with a 1.1ft @ 4s N slop underneath and a whisper of 0.6ft @ 13s dead-S groundswell (180°) that barely registers. Total energy ~8 kJ. Eight. That is knee-to-thigh, backwash-and-seaweed surf at every bank from Long Reef to Manly. The W offshore (268°, 19 kph gusting 36) will make it look pretty in photos and feel like nothing in the water. Then overnight a proper S groundswell lands: 6.8ft @ 9s from 183°, ~797 kJ by Thursday mid-morning — a hundred times today's energy. That 183° angle is dead south, which is exactly the direction Dee Why hates: the headland eats it and DY only pulls chest-to-head out of it while Long Reef sits overhead to well overhead on the same swell. Curl Curl splits the difference at chest-to-overhead. Wind Thursday is W offshore 7kt to about 11am then swings S/SE onshore — so it is a morning-only window. The weekend keeps it going: Saturday 5.5ft @ 10s from 167° (~462 kJ) and Sunday 5.7ft @ 11s from 149° (~758 kJ) with a clean NW/N offshore all Sunday morning — that 149° SSE angle finally feeds Dee Why properly. ✈️ Worth saying out loud: you fly to Oahu tomorrow, so Thursday's 797 kJ and the whole weekend run happen without you. Nothing lost today — it is 8 kJ. 🦈 SharkSmart live feeds (SMART drumline, DPI drone, SLSNSW, trauma, events) read clear — no Northern Beaches detections in the last 36h.

wind.summary: NW at dawn (330°, 13 kph) backing W then WSW through the morning — 19 kph gusting 36 by 10am. Straight offshore and gusty. It will hold the tiny faces up beautifully; there just isn't a face to hold up.

shark.summary: No shark alerts on the Northern Beaches (Palm Beach → Manly) in the last 36h. SMART drumline, DPI drone, SLSNSW, trauma and events feeds all read clear this morning.

days.label: Today
days.note: Skip it. ~8 kJ of energy is as close to flat as the Northern Beaches gets — 2.0ft @ 3s of WNW chop and a 0.6ft @ 13s dead-S trace that won't reach the bank. Knee-to-thigh everywhere, poor at all four spots. The W offshore (268°, 19 kph gusting 36) grooms it clean but there is nothing to groom. Save the energy: tomorrow brings ~797 kJ.

swells.label: Local wind chop — offshore-generated, no push at all
Weak ENE — the only workable angle, and it's tiny
Dead-S 13s trace — right on the shadow line, wraps to nothing here

dee-why.window: No real window. 7:00–9:00am off the 8:17am high is the least-bad hour if you just want to get wet. The Point has no swell to bend around it at 8 kJ.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: At 8 kJ your board choice can't save you — this is a longboard or nothing day. If you paddle out, go for the stretch and the water, not the waves. Tomorrow's dead-S 183° is the one to plan for, and at Dee Why that means the Point on the push, not the beachie.

long-reef.window: Marginally the best of four, which today means nothing. 7:00–9:00am on the high if you insist. The magnet needs swell to magnetise and there isn't any.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Long Reef is where tomorrow's dead-S 183° swell actually lands — overhead to well overhead on 797 kJ. Today it's knee-high. If you want a look, walk the headland and read the banks for the next swell instead of paddling out.

curl-curl.window: Nothing to work with. The W offshore is straighter here than at Dee Why but you'd be grooming ankle-slappers.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Curl Curl's lefts need swell height to bank up — 0–1ft won't do it. Worth remembering it goes chest-to-overhead tomorrow on the 183° S, which is a genuine backhand day.

manly.window: Effectively flat. Don't make the drive.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne is the most shadowed of the four and this is the day it shows — flat to knee. Even tomorrow's big S only pulls waist-to-chest here.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The swell of the week and you're on a plane. 6.8ft @ 9s from 183° dead south, ~797 kJ by mid-morning — a hundred times today's energy. Dead-S is Dee Why's weak angle so DY only makes chest-to-head while Long Reef runs overhead to well overhead. W offshore 7kt until roughly 11am then S/SE onshore kills it, so it's a morning-only window.

dee-why.window: 7:00–11:00am before the wind swings S/SE. The 183° dead-S is shadowed by the headland here — the Point is the only corner that turns it into a rideable wall.

long-reef.window: Pick of the coast. Full exposure to the 183° S — solid overhead-plus sets on 797 kJ. Dawn to 11am while the W holds.
alerts: Well overhead with 797 kJ behind it — step-up board, and pick your paddle channel before you jump in.

curl-curl.window: The sensible option — real size and punch without Long Reef's consequence. Best 7:30–10:30am.

manly.window: Shadowed as usual — waist-to-chest on a swell that's overhead at Long Reef. Only if the northern banks look too heavy.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Both days deliver and Sunday is better. Saturday: 5.5ft @ 10s from 167° SSE (~462 kJ) with a 1.8ft @ 7s E in the mix, light W offshore to about 11am then light E onshore. Sunday: 5.7ft @ 11s from 149° SSE (~758 kJ) with NW/N offshore holding all morning — and 149° is far enough off dead-south that Dee Why finally gets fed properly. Sunday mid-morning is the session of the weekend.

dee-why.window: Sunday 8:00–11:00am is the pick — 11s SSE at 149° actually wraps into the Point instead of being shadowed, with a clean NW offshore. Saturday is a touch smaller and softer on the 167° angle.

long-reef.window: Biggest of the four across both days. Sunday runs to 2ft overhead on 758 kJ with a N offshore — step-up territory, early.
alerts: Sunday 3–5ft with 758 kJ behind it — heavy paddle, size up.

curl-curl.window: Punchy both days, best Sunday dawn to mid-morning under the NW. Handles the size with less consequence than Long Reef.

manly.window: The manageable option. Clean chest-to-head Sunday morning, a size down on the northern banks as always.
